prayer-library.main-main-content-for-the: "For the continual prayer of a just man availeth much."
prayer-library.main-main-content-james-5: James 5:16 (Douay-Rheims), second half of the verse

prayer-library.main-main-content-how-thi: How This Library Is Sourced and Labeled
prayer-library.main-main-content-every-p: Every prayer here is either a traditional text long used in the Church, Scripture quoted from the public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision), or a brief cited reference to an official Church document such as the Catechism of the Catholic Church (cited by paragraph number rather than reproduced). We do not copy modern copyrighted prayer books or translations. Where a prayer is traditional and its English rendering varies between communities, we say so.
prayer-library.main-main-content-every-e: Every entry also carries an honest status line. "Church-attested" means an official act of the Church, such as an indulgence grant in the Enchiridion Indulgentiarum issued by the Apostolic Penitentiary. "Devotional tradition" means a practice or belief handed on by the faithful without that official weight. No prayer, novena, or devotion mechanically guarantees healing, money, a miracle, or any other specific outcome: prayer asks, and God remains free. Where a text itself speaks with confidence (as the Memorare does), we label that confidence as devotional, not as a Church guarantee.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-holy-are: Holy are You, O God. Holy are You, O Strong One. Holy are You, O Immortal One. Have mercy on us.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-in-syria: In Syriac tradition: Qadeeshat Aloho, Qadeeshat Hayeltono, Qadeeshat Lo Moyouto, etraham 'lain.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-adoratio: Adoration: the thrice-holy praise of God at the heart of Syriac worship, echoing the angels' cry in Isaiah 6:3.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-sing-or-: Sing or recite it slowly, standing, letting each of the three acclamations land before the plea for mercy.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-sung-in-: Sung in the Maronite Qurbono (Divine Liturgy), especially before the Gospel, and fitting any time as a short act of adoration; under a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-ancient-: Ancient Trisagion hymn of the Syriac churches, prayed in the Maronite liturgy for well over a millennium. Traditional; English renderings vary slightly between eparchies.
prayer-library.main-p-trisagion-reverenc: Reverence and recollection: tradition understands it as joining the worship of heaven rather than asking for anything.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-o-lord-a: O Lord and Master of my life, keep from me the spirit of indifference and discouragement, lust for power and idle chatter. Instead, grant to me, Your servant, the spirit of wholeness of being, humble-mindedness, patience, and love. O Lord and King, grant me the grace to be aware of my sins and not to judge my brother; for You are blessed, now and ever and forever. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-repentan: Repentance: it asks freedom from indifference, love of power, idle talk, and judging others, and asks for humility, patience, and love in their place.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-slowly-p: Slowly, phrase by phrase. In Syriac and Byzantine practice it is prayed with a prostration or deep bow after each petition; kneeling is a fitting substitute.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-daily-du: Daily during the Great Lent, morning and evening in Eastern usage; about two to three minutes, longer with prostrations.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-attribut: Attributed to Saint Ephrem the Syrian (d. 373), a deacon and doctor of the Church honored deeply in the Maronite tradition. Traditional English rendering.
prayer-library.main-p-st-ephrem-exactly-: Exactly what it petitions: self-knowledge, humility, patience, and freedom from judging others. Tradition treats it as the Church's school of Lent, not as a transaction.
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-from-t: From the Hymns of Saint Ephrem
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-there-: "There came out from Him water and blood; Adam washed and lived and returned to Paradise." And the refrain: "Blessed is He Who has quickened the dead of Sheol by His Cross!"
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-medita: Meditation on the Cross and on baptism: the water and blood from Christ's side washing humanity back into Paradise.
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-read-i: Read it slowly as lectio divina, then repeat the refrain several times and sit with it.
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-fittin: Fitting in Lent, Holy Week, and Eastertide, and at baptisms; five unhurried minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-saint-: Saint Ephrem the Syrian, Nisibene Hymns (Death and Satan before the Cross), public-domain English translation in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Series II, Vol. XIII (1898).
prayer-library.main-p-ephrem-hymn-gratit: Gratitude for baptism and hope in the resurrection, in the imagery of the greatest Syriac poet-theologian.
prayer-library.main-p-morning-offering-i: I offer You, O Lord, this day: my prayers, works, joys, and sufferings. May they rise before You like incense, through the intercession of the Mother of God and all the saints. Keep me in Your grace, and let Your will be done in me. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-morning-offering-t: To consecrate the whole day, including its work and its sufferings, before it begins.
prayer-library.main-p-morning-offering-o: On waking, before the phone and before work. Many families pray it aloud together.
prayer-library.main-p-morning-offering-t: Traditional morning offering as prayed in Maronite households; the exact formula varies by family and parish.
prayer-library.main-p-morning-offering-i: Intention: the day is handed over before it can take over. A devotional tradition, not a formula that binds the day to go well.
prayer-library.main-p-our-father-our-fat: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-our-father-the-pra: The prayer Christ himself taught: praise of the Father first, then petitions for bread, forgiveness, and deliverance. The Catechism calls it "the summary of the whole Gospel" (CCC 2761).
prayer-library.main-p-our-father-slowly-: Slowly, as a child speaking to a father. It opens every decade of the Rosary and anchors the Mass.
prayer-library.main-p-our-father-daily-i: Daily: in the liturgy, the Rosary, and morning and evening prayer; under a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-our-father-filial-: Filial trust: the Catechism teaches that this prayer forms us to ask as children, not as claimants (CCC 2777-2785).
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-hail-mar: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-praise-o: Praise of Mary in the words of Scripture, then a petition for her intercession now and at death.
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-unhurrie: Unhurriedly. In the Rosary, each Hail Mary is prayed while meditating on the mystery of its decade.
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-in-the-r: In the Rosary and the Angelus, and any time; seconds, or about twenty minutes for five decades.
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-luke-1-2: Luke 1:28 and 1:42 with the traditional closing petition, fixed in common use by the 16th century.
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-marian-t: Marian trust and humility. On the Rosary as a whole, see the
prayer-library.main-p-hail-mary-its-offi: ; its official indulgence grant is noted under the psalms and Scripture entries below.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-glory-be-: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; as it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-doxology-: Doxology: pure praise of the Trinity, asking nothing.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-simply-an: Simply and attentively; it closes each Rosary decade and many devotions.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-through-t: Through the day and in every Rosary; seconds.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-tradition: Traditional doxology (the Gloria Patri) of the early Church.
prayer-library.main-p-glory-be-a-habit-o: A habit of praise: it recenters prayer on God rather than on our requests.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-remember-: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection, implored thy help, or sought thy intercession was left unaided. Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my mother; to thee do I come, before thee I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in thy mercy hear and answer me. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-an-urgent: An urgent appeal for Mary's intercession in need.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-once-slow: Once, slowly, naming the need; traditionally repeated across the nine days of a novena.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-in-urgent: In urgent need, and at the hour of death; about a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-tradition: Traditional; its popular form is credited to Father Claude Bernard (17th century) and it is often linked in devotion with Saint Bernard of Clairvaux.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-confidenc: Confidence in approaching God through Mary's prayers.
prayer-library.main-p-memorare-the-line-: The line "never was it known" is devotional confidence, not a Church guarantee that every petition is granted as asked. The Church grants a partial indulgence for its devout recitation (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary) - a Church-attested grant about the prayer, not a promise about outcomes.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-soul: Soul of Christ, sanctify me. Body of Christ, save me. Blood of Christ, inebriate me. Water from the side of Christ, wash me. Passion of Christ, strengthen me. O good Jesus, hear me. Within Thy wounds hide me. Suffer me not to be separated from Thee. From the malignant enemy defend me. In the hour of my death call me, and bid me come unto Thee, that with Thy saints I may praise Thee for ever and ever. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-than: Thanksgiving and union with Christ's Passion, above all after receiving him in the Eucharist.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-sile: Silently and slowly, line by line, kneeling after Communion.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-imme: Immediately after Holy Communion; also in Passion meditation during Lent. Two to three minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-trad: Traditional; a 14th-century prayer long used in the Latin Church.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-grat: Gratitude and a felt nearness to the Passion, the school of self-giving love.
prayer-library.main-p-anima-christi-chur: Church-attested: a partial indulgence is granted for its devout recitation (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary).
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-o-my-go: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended Thee, and I detest all my sins because of Thy just punishments, but most of all because they offend Thee, my God, who art all-good and deserving of all my love. I firmly resolve, with the help of Thy grace, to sin no more and to avoid the near occasions of sin. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-to-expr: To express sorrow for sin and a resolve to change, resting on God's mercy.
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-after-a: After a quiet examination of conscience, slowly and meaning the resolution; aloud within the Sacrament of Penance when the priest invites it.
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-in-nigh: In nightly examination of conscience and in Confession; about a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-traditi: Traditional form; on contrition itself see the Catechism, CCC 1451-1454.
prayer-library.main-p-contrition-contrit: Contrition: "sorrow of the soul and detestation for the sin committed, together with the resolution not to sin again" (Council of Trent, cited in CCC 1451).
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-come-h: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of Thy faithful and enkindle in them the fire of Thy love. Send forth Thy Spirit and they shall be created, and Thou shalt renew the face of the earth. Let us pray: O God, who by the light of the Holy Spirit did instruct the hearts of the faithful, grant that by the same Holy Spirit we may be truly wise and ever enjoy His consolations. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-to-ask: To ask the Holy Spirit for wisdom and right judgment before acting.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-once-s: Once, slowly, before the task: study, a decision, a difficult conversation, or work.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-any-ti: Any time guidance is needed; especially fitting at Pentecost. About a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-tradit: Traditional invocation from the Pentecost liturgy of the Roman Missal.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-docili: Docility: the habit of asking before deciding.
prayer-library.main-p-holy-spirit-church: Church-attested: a partial indulgence is granted for this prayer (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary). The richer plenary grant on January 1 and Pentecost attaches to the Veni Creator hymn, a different text.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-prayer-: Prayer to Saint Michael the Archangel
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-saint-m: Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle; be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray; and do thou, O Prince of the Heavenly Host, by the power of God, cast into hell Satan and all the evil spirits who prowl about the world seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-to-ask-: To ask God's protection against spiritual evil through Saint Michael's intercession.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-once-at: Once, attentively; many parishes pray it together after Mass.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-after-m: After Mass, in temptation or spiritual distress, and any time; under a minute.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-compose: Composed by Pope Leo XIII in 1884 for the Leonine Prayers after Mass.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-confide: Confidence that evil is resisted by God's power, not ours.
prayer-library.main-p-st-michael-devotio: Devotional tradition only: no indulgence attaches to this prayer in the current Enchiridion, and it is a prayer of petition, not an exorcism or a guarantee of protection from harm.
prayer-library.main-p-healing-lord-jesus: Lord Jesus, You healed the sick who came to You in faith. Look on this illness with mercy. Give strength to the suffering, wisdom to those who care for them, and peace to those who wait. If it be Your will, restore health; in all things, keep us close to You. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-healing-intercessi: Intercession for the sick: strength for the suffering, wisdom for caregivers, and healing if God wills it.
prayer-library.main-p-healing-slowly-nam: Slowly, naming the person. It can be prayed daily through an illness, and joined to the
prayer-library.main-p-healing-in-illness: In illness, before surgery, and while waiting on diagnoses; a minute, daily if needed.
prayer-library.main-p-healing-peace-and-: Peace and solidarity: the sick are prayed with, not prayed at.
prayer-library.main-p-healing-no-prayer-: No prayer mechanically guarantees healing. The Catechism is explicit: "even the most intense prayers do not always obtain the healing of all illnesses" (CCC 1508). The Church's sacrament for the sick is the Anointing of the Sick (CCC 1499-1532); prayer supports, it does not control.
prayer-library.main-p-anxiety-be-nothing: "Be nothing solicitous: but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God. And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus." (Philippians 4:6-7, Douay-Rheims)
prayer-library.main-p-anxiety-to-hand-wo: To hand worry over to God and receive his peace.
prayer-library.main-p-anxiety-read-the-p: Read the passage slowly two or three times, then name the worry to God plainly and sit quietly.
prayer-library.main-p-anxiety-in-moments: In moments of worry, and as a morning or evening anchor; five minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-anxiety-the-passag: The passage itself names the fruit: "the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding." That is Scripture's own promise, received by faith, not a technique with a timer.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-the-lord-is-: "The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a contrite heart: and he will save the humble of spirit." (Psalm 33:19, Douay-Rheims) Lord, hold the one we have lost in Your light, and hold us in Your peace. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-to-grieve-wi: To grieve with God: entrusting the dead to him and asking peace for the living.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-read-the-ver: Read the verse, then speak the name of the one who died, then the petition. Praying it with others helps.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-after-a-loss: After a loss, at anniversaries, and in November, the Church's month of prayer for the dead; a few minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-scripture-pu: Scripture, public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner); the closing petition is traditional.
prayer-library.main-p-grief-consolation-: Consolation and hope. No devotion shortens grief on a schedule; the promise here is God's nearness, which the psalm itself attests.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-give-pra: "Give praise to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever." (Psalm 117:1, Douay-Rheims) Thank You, Lord, for this day and its gifts, known and unknown. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-thanksgi: Thanksgiving: naming God's goodness before asking for anything else.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-read-the: Read the verse, then name three concrete gifts of the day aloud.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-morning-: Morning or evening, daily; a minute or two.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-scriptur: Scripture, public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner); the closing line is traditional.
prayer-library.main-p-gratitude-joy-and-: Joy and attentiveness: gratitude trains the eye to notice mercy.
prayer-library.main-p-advent-come-lord-j: Come, Lord Jesus. Prepare our hearts as You prepared a dwelling in the Virgin's womb. Teach us to wait in hope, with Mary, for Your coming. Amen.
prayer-library.main-p-advent-to-learn-wa: To learn waiting: preparing for Christmas by hoping with Mary.
prayer-library.main-p-advent-as-a-short-: As a short daily aspiration through Advent, perhaps at an Advent wreath; pair with the
prayer-library.main-p-advent-the-four-we: The four weeks before Christmas; seconds each day.
prayer-library.main-p-advent-hopeful-pat: Hopeful patience in a season built on delay.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-pray-the-lent: Pray the Lenten Prayer of Saint Ephrem (above) daily, and the Miserere: "Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy. And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my iniquity." (Psalm 50:3, Douay-Rheims)
prayer-library.main-p-lent-repentance-le: Repentance: Lent's daily return to God.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-the-saint-eph: The Saint Ephrem prayer each morning and evening, and the Miserere slowly, verse by verse, when conscience is heavy.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-through-the-g: Through the Great Lent, especially weekdays; a few minutes daily.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-st-ephrem-pra: St Ephrem prayer (traditional); Psalm 50 from the public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-a-clean-heart: A clean heart, in the psalm's own words: honest repentance rather than vague regret.
prayer-library.main-p-lent-church-attest: Church-attested: a partial indulgence is granted for the devout recitation of the Miserere (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary).
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-feas: Feast of Saint Charbel (July 24 in the Maronite calendar)
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-and-: and, if you can, the nine-day novena leading to July 24. The feast falls on the third Sunday of July in the Maronite liturgical calendar, observed widely on July 24.
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-to-h: To honor Saint Charbel and ask his intercession, joining the worldwide devotion around his feast.
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-the-: The novena: the same prayer each day from July 15 to 23, a few minutes daily; on the feast itself, attend Mass if you can and pray the intercession prayer.
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-nove: Novena July 15-23; feast day July 24 (third Sunday of July in the Maronite calendar).
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-maro: Maronite liturgical calendar; novena practice is devotional tradition.
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-clos: Closeness to Saint Charbel's example of silence, prayer, and Eucharistic devotion.
prayer-library.main-p-feast-charbel-chur: Church-attested: the Church grants a partial indulgence to those who recite an approved prayer in honor of a saint on his feast day (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, "Veneration of the Saints"). Healings attributed to Saint Charbel's intercession belong to devotional tradition and individual testimony; none is promised, and the Church investigates claims rigorously before calling anything miraculous.
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-glory-to: "Glory to God in the highest: and on earth peace to men of good will." (Luke 2:14, Douay-Rheims) In the Maronite tradition, the Christmas season extends through Epiphany (Denho) on January 6.
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-to-adore: To adore the newborn Christ with the angels' own words.
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-sing-or-: Sing or recite the Gloria verse at the crib or the tree, and linger over it rather than rushing to presents.
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-december: December 25 through January 6 (Epiphany, Denho, in the Maronite calendar).
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-luke-2-1: Luke 2:14, public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision); Maronite liturgical calendar.
prayer-library.main-p-christmas-joy-the-: Joy: the season's whole point, received not manufactured.
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-l: Lord, I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof; but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. (cf. Matthew 8:8, prayed at every Mass)
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-h: Humility and readiness before receiving the Eucharist.
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-s: Silently with the whole congregation just before receiving, then again quietly in your pew.
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-a: At every Mass, immediately before Communion; seconds.
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-t: The liturgy of the Mass, from the centurion's words in Matthew 8:8.
prayer-library.main-p-before-communion-r: Reverence: receiving as a gift, never as a right.
prayer-library.main-p-after-communion-pr: Pray the Anima Christi (above), the Church's classic thanksgiving after Communion.
prayer-library.main-p-after-communion-th: Thanksgiving while the gift is still warm.
The Anima Christi slowly, kneeling, before the conversation and the parking lot reclaim you.
prayer-library.main-p-after-communion-in: In the quiet minutes after receiving; two to three minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-after-communion-ch: Church-attested: the Anima Christi carries a partial indulgence (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary).
prayer-library.main-p-before-confession-: Pray Come, Holy Spirit (above), then examine your conscience quietly and pray the Act of Contrition (above) before entering the Sacrament of Penance.
Preparation: an honest conscience and a willing heart before the sacrament.
Invoke the Holy Spirit, review the commandments and your life since your last confession, then pray the Act of Contrition.
Before each confession; ten quiet minutes serves better than two rushed ones.
Traditional practice; the Catechism treats contrition and confession at CCC 1451-1498.
The sacrament's own grace: forgiveness and peace, received through the Church, not through the prayer alone.
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-psalm-22-: Psalm 22 - The Lord Is My Shepherd (Douay-Rheims numbering: Psalm 22)
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-the-lord-: "The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. He hath set me in a place of pasture. He hath brought me up, on the water of refreshment: he hath converted my soul. He hath led me on the paths of justice, for his own name's sake. For though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evils, for thou art with me. Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me."
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-trust-whe: Trust when the path is dark: God's guidance through uncertainty, illness, and death.
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-as-lectio: As lectio divina: read it through, then again one verse at a time, resting on the verse that stops you.
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-in-uncert: In uncertainty and illness, and at funerals; five unhurried minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-psalm-22-: Psalm 22 (23 in most modern Bibles), public-domain Douay-Rheims Bible (Challoner revision).
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-trust-the: Trust: the psalm does not deny the shadow; it denies the aloneness inside it.
prayer-library.main-p-psalm-22-church-at: Church-attested: reading Scripture with reverence carries a partial indulgence, and a plenary indulgence when done for at least half an hour, under the usual conditions (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum, Apostolic Penitentiary).
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-blessed: "Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land. Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted."
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-to-let-: To let Christ's own definition of happiness correct ours.
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-read-sl: Read slowly and stop at the beatitude that resists you; that one is yours to carry today.
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-any-sea: Any season, especially when priorities feel scrambled; five minutes.
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-the-pro: The promises named are Christ's own, kingdom-shaped rather than circumstance-shaped: comfort, inheritance, mercy.
prayer-library.main-p-beatitudes-church-: Church-attested: as above, devout Scripture reading carries a partial indulgence, plenary for half an hour or more under the usual conditions (Enchiridion Indulgentiarum).
prayer-library.main-prayers-of-the-saint: A traditional prayer for each saint on this site, with its source and an honest note on who wrote it.
prayer-library.main-main-content-interce: Intercession prayers, a nine-day novena framework, and daily invocations through Saint Charbel.
prayer-library.main-main-content-a-visua: A visual guide to the beads, the mysteries, and the order of prayer.
prayer-library.main-main-content-pray-ea: Pray each mystery with guided text, voice, and a hands-free timer.
prayer-library.main-main-content-daily-p: Daily practices inspired by Saint Charbel's silence, fasting, and Eucharistic devotion.
prayer-library.main-main-content-a-short: A short email every morning at 6 AM - a prayer, the day's rosary, and a prayer to Saint Charbel.
prayer-library.footer-div-prayer-library: Prayer library compiled from traditional and public-domain sources; translation, usage, and status notes appear under each entry. Author: Please pray for the person who made this website.
prayer-library.main-find-a-prayer-sick-a: sick, anxiety, students, family, miracle, rosary...
